correctness.rationale: Both three-dimensional branch Jacobians are explicitly monomial, with determinant of magnitude two. For right-count \(t\not\equiv0\pmod3\), their product is a single three-cycle and every eigenvalue modulus is \(2^{n/3}\). For \(t=3q\), the derivative is diagonal with exponent vector \((q+c_0,q+c_1,q+c_2)\) up to order, where \(c_j\) is a nonnegative left-count by right-prefix residue. Hence \(\chi_n\ge2^{1/n}\) for \(n\ge4\), with equality precisely for \(t=3\) and at least one empty cyclic L-gap. Counting marked right symbols gives \(n/3[\binom{n-1}{2}-\binom{n-4}{2}]=n(n-3)\). A proper-power word would be repeated three times and have equal positive gaps, so every minimizer is primitive and there are \(n-3\) cycles. Exact rational checker reconstructed every nontrivial word for n=1..9 (13177 assertions) and confirmed multiplicities; the symbolic bijection itself is supported by the primary full text, not mere finite tests.
